text:
alex: FYI: after yesterday's selector tweak I see host CPU up on ingress nodes. p95 tokenization + parse climbed ~28% in the canary window.

maria: rough. any flamegraph or counters yet? is this purely tokenization or something upstream (streaming/GRPC)?

alex: quick flame excerpt:
```
CPU 90s sample
  tokenize/ingress.go:splitTokens    24s  (26%)
  parse/request.go:parseFrame        12s  (13%)
  grpc/writer.go:emitFrame           9s  (10%)
  kvcache/lookup.go:batchFetch       4s  (4%)
  kernel/selector.go:chooseVariant   3s  (3%)
```

ken: hmmm. chooseVariant shouldn't be heavy. Did selector change pick smaller variants more often? smaller model variants -> more frequent frame flushes perhaps.

alex: selector counts: medium->small jumped from 8% -> 37% in the canary. kv hit-rate dipped ~2.8% during that interval.

sophie: we rolled an optimization to favor "kernel_low_latency" which biases toward small input-friendly kernels. Might be interacting with the streaming flush policy.

maria: do we have socket write size histograms? small writes + syscalls amplify host cost.

alex: grabbed tcp_write_size histogram and grpc small-write counter. 10m window (canary):
```
write_size_bytes: median=140, p95=396, small_writes(<256)=61% (baseline 19%)
grpc_small_writes/s: 312 -> 910 (canary)
```

ken: that's the smoking gun. selector change increased small-frame frequency which triggered more write syscalls and more parsing churn. Also note slight kv hit dip could be due to variant-specific cache keys (we add model tag to cache key).

sophie: quick mitigation: revert the kernel bias flag in the canary and bump minibatch window to improve coalescing. Also consider a host-side coalesce guard: don't flush unless buffered >512B or timeout reached.

infra-bot: deploy-canary sophie/revert-kernel-bias -> ingress-canary-3 started at 1777710005 :rocket:

alex: after 12min: parse CPU -20%, small writes -53%, kv hit-rate returned to baseline. p99 tail stable.

maria: good. action items:
- add unit test reproducing fragmented input when selector forces small variants (simulate streaming byte boundaries)
- add metric: parse_bytes/request and grpc_coalesce_misses/s
- make grpc writer have a soft-coalesce threshold (configurable, default 512)

ken: I'll investigate selector heuristics: avoid over-weighting kernel_low_latency when it would increase host transmit operations. Maybe add cost term for "expected host write ops". Filed INF-4832.

sophie: also worth visiting KV key shape. If variant name appended to key greatly increases key length, we might cause cold shards or higher memcmp cost. Ken, can you send sample keys?

ken: yep will dump anonymized keys. early look shows we append "_sm" suffix for small variant which increases avg key len by ~6 bytes. Not huge but combined with more requests could matter.

alex: plan for next week: prototype selector with a host-framing penalty in cost function, run 1h A/B with streaming-heavy traces. If stable, roll selector with coalesce fallback.

sophie: sounds good. +1 on coalesce fallback as fast patch.

infra-bot: canary completed at 1777710300 white_check_mark 3/3 healthy.

maria: will add a short postmortem note describing "selector-host framing interaction" so others are aware. This caught us since kernel costs were optimized in isolation.

ken: INF-4832 assigned to runtime/selector squad. alex will own the coalesce writer PR.

alex: creating PR and test case now. thanks for the quick rollback help.

sophie: good catch all. these cross-layer interactions are tricky; add a checklist item for future kernel changes: "simulate streaming burden" in perf harness.
